summary.headline: Marksans Q2 FY27 record revenue of INR940 crores (+30.5% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 22.8%, with UK and Europe up 65%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a record quarter: revenue from operations rose 30.5% YoY to INR940 crores and EBITDA rose 48.3% to INR214 crores, with margin up 274 bps to 22.8%, above the 20-21% guidance range. Management said ex-QliniQ underlying growth was about 25%, with UK and Europe (up 65%) and Australia and New Zealand (up 64%) offsetting a slower North America (+8.7%). Profit after tax rose 44.8% YoY to INR144 crores but fell sequentially from INR159 crores, due to new amortisation of acquired intangibles, lower other income and a higher tax rate. H1 free cash flow was INR275 crores and net cash reached INR1,095 crores.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Revenue INR421 crores, 44.8% of Q2 revenue, a record quarter but up only 8.7% YoY; management cited US affordability pressure and seasonality. Order book is $225 million, targeted at $300 million within three years.

segments.name: UK and Europe
segments.commentary: Revenue up 65% YoY to about INR405 crores (43% of revenue); ex-acquisitions growth was 49%. QliniQ (Netherlands) contributed about INR84 crores in H1. ABCnow and Marksans GmbH are building the German platform.

segments.name: Australia and New Zealand
segments.commentary: Revenue up 64% YoY to about INR101 crores (10.7% of revenue), all through the Nova subsidiary's branded Rx business. Target is a $100 million subsidiary within three years.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR14 crores (1.5% of revenue), hit by Middle East disruption and shipment timing. Management sees a possible recovery to INR20-25 crores per quarter if conditions ease.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin for Q3 and Q4 guided at 55-56%, down from 58.5% in Q2, as inventory costs rise.
EBITDA margin expected in the 21-22% range for the rest of the year.
PAT expected to be broadly in line with expectations, after tax provisions and higher depreciation; management said the full-year trajectory is range-bound.
Revenue run-rate is close to INR1,000 crores per quarter; management said it expects to reach INR4,000 crores next year and INR5,000 crores within three years.
Long-term aims: about INR6,000 crores in revenue within five years, and Europe at about INR1,000 crores in five years.
Dividend: about one-third of free cash flow, in line with history, per CFO; the board has not yet decided on FY27.
capex_capacity: Plans to add blocks at the Teva plant in India for new dosage forms and debottlenecking.
Also in dialogue with two companies on acquiring a manufacturing plant in India; timeline about 12 months. Dosage forms under review are not injectables, and solid oral will be included.
Current capacity is adequate for about two to three years for oral solids, per management.
Depreciation rose by about INR6-7 crores QoQ after intangibles were moved to a finite 10-year life; management said this is the run-rate for the next couple of quarters.
Lease liabilities rose by about INR120 crores on a new UK lease.
demand_pricing: US price erosion in prescription products is in single digits; no finished-product price increases seen in the base portfolio.
Mix is about 75% OTC and 25% Rx; H1 growth was largely volume-driven, per CFO.
New launches are expected to contribute about 10% of US growth, 20% of UK and 50-60% of Europe.
Five or six ANDA filings are planned by March; R&D targets niche and complex molecules, including topicals and liquids.
API price pressure (paracetamol, ibuprofen) is elevated; management expects cooling in about 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why is US constant-currency growth low in H1, and what is the second-half outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonality (cold season in Oct-Dec) and affordability pressure from inflation and oil prices. It reiterated the target of a $300 million order book within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 PAT exceed H1 given Q1 benefited from low-cost inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA should stay in the 21-22% range and PAT should be broadly in line; it did not commit to H2 above H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the Indian capacity expansion and the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion will come through new blocks at the Teva plant and possibly an acquired plant, with dialogue on two companies. Timeline is about 12 months; no backward integration into API.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation run-rate after the intangibles change?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said intangibles are now amortised over 10 years, which covers QliniQ and ABCnow acquired intangibles. Management confirmed the current quarterly run-rate continues for the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ROW and is INR20-25 crores per quarter achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Middle East disruption is easing, and INR20-25 crores per quarter is achievable if conditions improve, with full recovery hoped for by year-end. It declined to forecast geopolitics.

qa_highlights.question: Will gross margin stay near 58% or fall to 55-56% in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 55-56% for Q3 and Q4, and said margins would recover if raw material prices fall.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from higher inventory and freight costs; freight costs nearly doubled and added about INR20 crores QoQ to other expenses.
Middle East and Red Sea logistics disruption affecting ROW shipments; Q3 is the seasonally strong US quarter.
Sequential PAT decline from amortisation of acquired intangibles, lower other income and a 25.8% tax rate.
US growth is slow (+8.7%) with price erosion in single digits and affordability pressure.
Capital deployment: cash is earmarked for European M&A (possibly within 12 months), an Indian plant acquisition, and capex; buyback is only an option.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and the multi-year targets, but cautious on the near-term margin and geopolitical outlook. Management was direct that Q2 margins benefited from Q1 low-cost inventory and declined to predict geopolitics or the dividend.
key_quotes: Q2 was a record quarter for us, with revenue from operations reaching INR940 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 30.5%.
We believe we will be range-bound overall for the year.
Retailers will not ask for a price cut, but our gross margin will increase, obviously, or will come back to its historic numbers if we see raw material prices coming down.
Historically, like, 1/3 of our free cash flow generation, we have been distributing as dividend. Broadly, it will be in line with that.

growth.why: Management expects revenue of about INR4,000 crores next year and INR5,000 crores within three years, backed by a US order book of $225 million (target $300 million), new launches and Teva-plant blocks plus a possible plant acquisition in ~12 months, but no specific INR-capacity timeline for the INR4,000 crore target was given; Q3-Q4 EBITDA margin guided at 21-22% with gross margin 55-56%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin guided down to 55-56% from 58.5% in Q2 and EBITDA margin guided at 21-22% versus 22.8% in Q2, as inventory costs rise and Q1 low-cost inventory benefit fades.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New blocks at the Teva plant are planned and a plant acquisition in India is in dialogue with a ~12-month timeline, but no INR capacity timeline was given for the INR4,000 crore target, and current oral solids capacity is adequate for 2-3 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 growth was largely volume-driven, the US order book is $225 million (target $300 million in 3 years), and ROW could recover to INR20-25 crores per quarter, though North America grew only 8.7% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it is already planning for INR5,000 crores and looking at infrastructure expansion, with cash earmarked for capex and an Indian plant acquisition; utilisation was not disclosed, so this rests on stated plans rather than a utilisation read.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held EBITDA margin at 21-22% and PAT only 'broadly in line', declined to commit to H2 above H1, and guided gross margin down to 55-56%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gross margin is guided down 250-350 bps from Q2, freight costs nearly doubled (about INR20 crores QoQ), Middle East disruption hits ROW, and North America grew just 8.7%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Five or six ANDA filings are planned by March, and new launches are expected to add about 10% of US growth, 20% of UK and 50-60% of Europe.

rows.label: Australia/NZ to USD100m subsidiary via Nova
rows.why: ANZ revenue rose 64% YoY to about INR101 crores (10.7% of Q2 revenue) through Nova's branded Rx business, and management targets a USD100 million subsidiary within three years.

rows.label: European M&A deployment
rows.why: Net cash of INR1,095 crores is earmarked for European acquisitions (possibly within 12 months) and an Indian plant, with buyback only an option.

rows.label: API price relief (paracetamol, ibuprofen)
rows.why: API prices are elevated, and management expects cooling in about 30 days, which could ease gross margin pressure from the 55-56% guide.

tone.note: Management was confident on the multi-year targets (INR4,000 crores next year, $300m order book, Europe growth) but cautious on near-term gross margin, freight costs, and the US affordability-driven slowdown; analysts pressed on H2 versus H1 PAT and the sustainability of the 58% gross margin.
